items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: nobody was happy about that situation except Randy and Bank who didn't care and were close buddies.

ctx.x: But about two weeks after we were on tour, Zutty went into his act which I was afraid he would do, when Lily wrote to me in Germany and told me that she had engaged him for the tour. I knew he had a reputation for being moody and difficult to work with. He would be at times very unpleasant. It was a pity, because he and Marge were such jolly people when you didn't have to work with them, started to be real drags, staying for themselves, refusing friendly advances. They had an old dog named "Bring Down" travelling…

Zutty couldn't stand the pianist, and every night was growling about...that sh...pianist. He would slow down the tempo terribly, and if I said something, try to put the blame on Randy. He was making me feel miserable, and nobody was happy about that situation except Randy and Bank who didn't care and were close buddies. Those two were always up to some foolishness.

One night, it was almost 9 p.m., and they had not shown up at the theatre. Somebody told me that they had been seen in an amusement park near the theatre and that they were riding a Merry-go-round. I went to check and effectively found them having a ball on a merry-go-round for kids, wearing two long bonnets, one green, one red.
